# NLP501-bench v1: the team's one benchmark

**Status:** agreed by the team on 2026-10-30 and frozen in `data/eval/benchmark_v1.json`.
**Results:** `docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md`, generated by `python -m app.eval.benchmark report`.

## Why one benchmark, and why it mixes both datasets

The project had two datasets, built in parallel: ours on `feature/*` and Đán's on `coding`.

- **Each defined "relevant" its own way.** Ours uses two LLM annotators judging each pair holistically. Đán's uses a
  rubric (`gold_spec`) close to his own scoring.
- **So each system won on its own data.** Neither number alone could say which version was better.

v1 fixes this. It keeps both datasets and gives the whole team **one split, one official number and one command**:

| | dev (tuning allowed) | test (locked; the official number) |
|---|---|---|
| ours: 50 CVs, silver labels | JD-001, 002, 003, 006, 008, 012 | JD-004, 005, 007, 009, 010, 011 |
| coding: 200 CVs, rubric gold, commit `6991c3d` | ambiguous_junior, mobile_offshore | ambiguous_senior, bank_api_qa, fpt_automation_test, startup_framework |

**How the split was chosen:**
- **Ours:** stratified by company type with seed 501 (`benchmark.split_ours`). That gives one test JD per type plus
  two at random.
- **Coding:** keeps the dev/test split Đán pre-registered in `gold.json`.
- **Coverage:** both splits contain an ambiguous or vague JD. Test also holds the Vietnamese JD (JD-010).

## Rules

1. **Each JD ranks the CVs labelled for it,** that is, its own source's pool. Cross pairs (our JD × Đán's CV) have no
   labels and are never scored.
2. **Both label sets use the same 0–3 scale:**
   - 0 = not relevant;
   - 1 = weak;
   - 2 = would phone-screen;
   - 3 = would interview.
3. **The official number is nDCG@10 over the 10 test JDs**, with a 95% bootstrap CI and the per-source breakdown. P@5,
   R@20 and τ are reported alongside.
4. **Tuning only on dev.** Any change to retrieval, chunking, extraction, prompts or scoring is decided on dev, then
   reported on test, once.
5. **Same conditions for every system:**
   - the same JD requirements (extracted once, shared);
   - the same LLM (Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5);
   - `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`;
   - the same metrics code.
6. **Frozen.** The manifest pins every input file by SHA-256 (268 files) and the coding branch's commit.
   `python -m app.eval.benchmark verify` and `tests/test_benchmark.py` fail if anything changes.
7. **A change is a new version.** New labels or data mean v1.1 or v2, with a new manifest. Old results stay comparable
   only within their version. The first planned change: the human-adjudicated labels (`docs/labeling/`) replace the
   silver ones as **v1.1**.

## Honest caveats

- **The lock is new.** Results on these JDs were seen before the split existed, during v1–v3.1 development. From now on,
  test is locked.
- **Two definitions of relevance remain:** silver labels and rubric gold. They are kept apart in the per-source
  columns. The completed 120-pair human audit puts the rounded silver mean at κ = 0.695/0.661 against Hoa/Phúc, so
  the silver set is secondary rather than a substitute for people (`docs/HUMAN_LABELS.md`).
- **10 test JDs give wide intervals** (about ±0.05–0.08). Differences under about 0.03 are not significant.
- **The Djinni pilot is separate.** Its 424-pair Aggregate Human Gold checks real text but does not repair the old
  split or enlarge the official 10-JD test. Results must stay in a separate external-validity table.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd backend && export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 LLM_PROVIDER=claude_code
uv run python -m app.eval.benchmark verify                        # inputs intact?
uv run python -m app.eval.run retrieval --bench ours && uv run python -m app.eval.run retrieval --bench coding
uv run python -m app.eval.run agent --systems P6,B4                # agent on ours
export DATA_DIR=$(uv run python -m app.eval.bench materialize | cut -d= -f2)   # agent on the coding corpus
uv run python -m app.rag.ingest && uv run python -m app.eval.run agent --bench coding --systems P6,B4 \
    --jds ambiguous_senior,bank_api_qa,fpt_automation_test,startup_framework
unset DATA_DIR && uv run python -m app.rag.ingest                  # back to our corpus
git worktree add --detach /tmp/coding 6991c3d && uv run python -m app.eval.benchmark dan-core --src /tmp/coding
uv run python -m app.eval.benchmark report                          # → docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md
```

## v2: v1 + a real-data test layer (Djinni)

**Status:** frozen in `data/eval/benchmark_v2.json` (`python -m app.eval.benchmark_v2 freeze`).
**Results:** `docs/BENCHMARK_V2_RESULTS.md`, generated by `python -m app.eval.benchmark_v2 report`.

v1 had two weaknesses a reviewer named: 10 test JDs give wide intervals, and every CV is synthetic. v2 keeps v1 exactly
(its manifest, split and labels are untouched and still reported on their own) and adds to **test only**:

| | dev | test |
|---|---|---|
| djinni: 250 real anonymised CVs (Djinni Recruitment Dataset, MIT), coding commit `a0a4c1a` | — | 8 English QA Automation JDs (4 stacks × levels) |

- **Pooled labels.** 424 (JD, CV) pairs: per JD the union of four rankers' top 20 plus 10 random CVs
  (`labeling/pool.json`). Metrics on Djinni are **condensed**: a ranking is scored over its judged CVs only.
- **Labels.** Silver for now: the mean of two blind LLM annotators (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5) with the same rubric as
  `scripts/llm_label.py`. The team's human labels (`labels_A.xlsx`, `labels_B.xlsx`, adjudicated) replace them as
  **v2.1**; `docs/DJINNI_LABELS.md` reports κ between humans and between humans and silver.
- **Labelling tool.** `python -m app.eval.djinni review` writes `.runtime/bench/djinni/labeling/review.html`: every
  pooled pair, JD next to CV, keys 0–3, autosave, export to JSON for `djinni import`. Two modes, recorded per label
  (`saw_model`): **blind** (the annotator's own judgement; what counts as human validation) and **review** (Opus 5.5's
  grade and evidence from `data/eval/djinni_gold_opus.json` shown; anchored, so reported as such). The Opus close read
  (8 CVs a call) is a model annotator: it is never mixed into the silver mean that v2 pins.
- **Blind page and subset.** `review.html?blind=1` hides the mode switch and Opus's grades, unlocks grading 20 s after a pair opens and asks for a note on every 1 or 2. `&subset=1` shows the stratified 80-pair sample (`djinni.subset`: 10 per JD at even steps of the silver mean, so every grade level is in it; the annotator is not told which). 80 pairs are enough for a human–human κ; they are not a full gold.
- **Annotator quality check** (`djinni.qc_problems`, run by `djinni score`). Human labels count towards gold only if the annotator reaches weighted κ ≥ 0.4 with at least one other annotator and, for blind labels, a median of ≥ 10 s per pair (the page stamps every grade). A set that fails stays in `data/eval/` and in the agreement table, marked excluded.
- **Real CVs stay out of `data/`** (repo rule): `python -m app.eval.djinni fetch` copies them from git into
  `.runtime/bench/djinni`; only labels are committed.
- **18 test JDs** in v2 (6 ours + 4 coding + 8 djinni). Nothing is tuned on Djinni.

```bash
cd backend && export PYTHONHASHSEED=0 LLM_PROVIDER=claude_code
uv run python -m app.eval.djinni fetch
uv run python -m app.eval.djinni silver --tag a --model claude_code:claude-opus-5-5
uv run python -m app.eval.djinni silver --tag b --model claude_code:claude-sonnet-5-5
uv run python -m app.eval.run retrieval --bench djinni
export DATA_DIR=$(uv run python -m app.eval.bench materialize djinni | cut -d= -f2)
QDRANT_URL=:memory: uv run python -m app.eval.run agent --bench djinni --systems P6,B4 && unset DATA_DIR
uv run --group ml python -m app.eval.finetune score            # adds the fine-tuned reranker (E20) on all sources
uv run python -m app.eval.benchmark_v2 report
```
